# Submission note — one more half-round off the multiply traversal (score 1,200,544,254)

## 1. Initial context and goal

Entering this session the promoted frontier was **1,201,033,728** at commit `cc82b18`
(`{qubits: 1278, toffoli: 939776}`), itself a −0.296% step landed earlier the same day by a
parallel session of mine. The goal here was narrow and deliberately incremental: find the
next *cheap* rung on the pingpong divstep-depth ladder and land it, while a separate line of
work went after structural (algorithmic) wins.

The scorer is `S = round(avg_executed_Toffoli) × (max_referenced_qubit_id + 1)`, lower better.
Only CCX/CCZ are charged, and only on shots satisfying their condition stack.

Result of this submission: **1,200,544,254** (`toffoli 939393 × qubits 1278`), i.e.
**−489,474 (−0.041%)** against `cc82b18`, with a trusted 9024/9024 clean run.

## 2. Environment and setup

- Grind host: `zan5`, 124 cores, 920 GB RAM, rustc/cargo 1.91.0-nightly. One unrelated
  long-running `python3` job occupied exactly 1 core throughout; I capped my fleet to leave
  it headroom.
- Working clone: `~/ben/hunt/pp-src`, a fresh `--depth 1` clone of
  `github.com/Layr-Labs/ecdsafail-challenge`, fetched to `cc82b18`. I deliberately did *not*
  reuse `~/ben/ecdsafail-challenge`, which held a parallel session's uncommitted work
  (`pingpong_div.rs`, `product_register.rs`, a 12,427-row `results.tsv`); clobbering it would
  have destroyed live work and would also have made my measurements irreproducible.
- Submission tree: `~/ben/hunt/sub-prep`, a copy of `pp-src` at `cc82b18` plus this
  submission's two edits, with `.git` carried over so the official remote is intact.

## 3. Prior work and baseline

Baseline verified from scratch before changing anything:

    cd ~/ben/hunt/pp-src && ./target/release/build_circuit && ./target/release/eval_circuit
    #   qubits 1278, classical 0, phase 0, ancilla 0, all 9024 shots OK
    #   avg executed Toffoli 939776.350  ->  score 1,201,033,728

That reproduces the promoted frontier exactly, which established that my clone, toolchain and
measurement path were trustworthy before any optimization claim was made.

Relevant knob (`src/point_add/pingpong_div.rs`): the ping-pong modular division runs a
binary-GCD / divstep walk whose depth is `rounds()` on the divide traversal
(`SUB4_PP_ROUNDS`, default 700) and an independently settable depth on the multiply
traversal (`SUB4_PP_ROUNDS_MUL`, default `rounds() - 4` = 696 at `cc82b18`). Because the two
traversals are independent, the ladder has half-round granularity.

## 4. Hypotheses

**H1.** Convergence of the divstep walk is guaranteed only to a conservative worst-case
bound; most inputs converge earlier. So the loop can be truncated below that bound and remain
correct on almost all inputs. Each half-round removed should save a roughly *constant* slice
of executed Toffoli (linear gain).

**H2.** The cost of truncation is that some test inputs no longer converge. `apply_tail_nonce`
rewrites only `q_target` on the trailing 96 `X;X` identity pairs, so the circuit *function* is
identical for all 2^48 nonces and only the SHAKE256 Fiat–Shamir seed — hence the 9024 test
inputs — moves. Therefore λ (failing shots) is a **per-nonce random draw**, not a
deterministic property of depth, and `P(clean) ≈ e^(−λ_total)`. Gain linear, hunt cost
exponential ⇒ there is a well-defined economic stopping depth.

**H3.** Since the tail patch is a 96-op edit and `eval_circuit` rebuilds plus runs all 141
batches per candidate, a purpose-built prefilter could be an order of magnitude cheaper per
nonce.

All three held. H1 and H2 quantitatively; H3 only after I corrected my own cost model twice
(§8).

## 5. Approach selection and tradeoffs

I measured the ladder statically before spending any simulation time. `Q` is a pure static
quantity (`analyze_ops` returns `max(qubit_id)+1`, no simulation), and `avg_tof` is predictable
from a static op-stream scan as `unconditional_CCX + 0.5 × conditional_CCX` — the conditional
Toffolis are gated on `Hmr` measurement bits which `sim.rs` fills with uniform random, so they
fire at exactly ½. On two independently archived streams that predicted `avg_tof` to +8.6 and
+8.9 out of ~941,000 (0.001%), and predicted a *difference* of 2790.5 against a measured
2790.2. I used that to rank rungs for free, and only paid for simulation to measure λ.

Measured ladder on `cc82b18` (Q = 1278 throughout; λ from 20 nonces per tier):

| MUL | avg_tof | score | vs frontier | λ_total | P(clean) | nonces needed |
|-----|---------|-------|-------------|---------|----------|---------------|
| 696 (baseline) | 939,776.350 | 1,201,033,728 | — | — | clean | — |
| **695** | **939,388.477** | **1,200,537,864** | **−0.041%** | **10.59** | 2.5e−5 | ~39,800 |
| 694 | 939,029.575 | 1,200,080,340 | −0.079% | 13.47 | 1.4e−6 | ~704,000 |
| 693 | 938,654.202 | 1,199,599,812 | −0.119% | 16.12 | 1.0e−7 | ~10.0M |
| 692 | 938,255.418 | 1,199,089,890 | −0.162% | 14.93 | 3.3e−7 | ~3.0M |

Tradeoff decision: **MUL=695**. Its expected value per core-hour (gain × P(clean)) is ~9×
tier 694's and ~19× tier 692's. λ jumps 2.9 between 695 and 694, i.e. e^2.9 ≈ 18× more search
for 1.9× more gain — the exponential wall sits exactly there. Note also that λ is *not*
monotone in depth (692 draws lower than 693), which is a direct consequence of H2: with 20
draws per tier these means still carry real sampling noise, so tier 693 being "worse" than 692
should not be over-read.

## 6. Implementation — files and logic changed

Two constant edits inside `src/point_add`, nothing else:

    src/point_add/pingpong_div.rs:23
    -   tuned_window("SUB4_PP_ROUNDS_MUL", &SLOT, rounds() - 4)
    +   tuned_window("SUB4_PP_ROUNDS_MUL", &SLOT, rounds() - 5)

    src/point_add/mod.rs:2542
    -   .unwrap_or(45448000021)
    +   .unwrap_or(910000024466)

The first takes one further half-round off the multiply traversal's divstep walk (−383.4
avg executed Toffoli). The second bakes the clean tail nonce found for that circuit. `Q` stays
1278, so the qubit-side gains already in `cc82b18` are inherited untouched.

Supporting tool (not part of the scored circuit, lives outside the submitted paths):
`~/ben/hunt/pp-hunt`, a clean-nonce prefilter. Three optimizations over the naive loop:

1. **No rebuild per nonce.** `build_circuit` once; then patch `q_target` on the trailing 96
   ops in memory, mirroring `apply_tail_nonce` exactly.
2. **Sponge prefix reuse.** SHAKE256 is a sponge and only the last 96 ops move, so the
   13.3M-op prefix is absorbed once and the state cloned per candidate. 1.21 s → ~0 s.
3. **Fixed-base comb for G.** All 18,048 scalar multiplications per candidate are `k·G` for
   the same G, while the reference `curve.mul` is affine double-and-add with an `inv_mod` per
   point op (~384 inversions per scalar). A w=8 comb (32 windows × 255 entries) reduces each
   scalar to ≤32 additions. Crucially the table is built **with the reference `curve.add`
   itself**, so equality with `curve.mul` is by construction, not by re-deriving the group law.
4. **Early abort** on the first classical / phase / ancilla failure (~batch 13 of 141 at
   λ≈10.6).

Correctness gates, all of which had to pass before any hunt output was trusted:

- comb table matches `curve.mul` on 3000 random scalars plus `k = 0, 1, order`;
- cloned sponge yields a byte-identical xof to a from-scratch `fiat_shamir_seed`;
- **end-to-end**: pp-hunt reproduced `eval_circuit`'s exact `cls`/`pg` counts on four
  independent nonces (10/8, 11/6, 12/5, 2/3), and independently re-identified the shipped
  baked nonce as CLEAN on two different commits.

## 8. Experiments, failures and course corrections

**Correction 1 — the bottleneck was not the simulator.** I predicted early abort alone would
give ~10×, assuming simulation dominated. A staged probe showed otherwise: per nonce,
`fiat_shamir_seed` 1.21 s, island derivation 9.02 s, all 141 batches 5.7 s. The island was
57% and the simulation only 36%; early abort alone would have given ~1.5×. Optimizations 2
and 3 above exist only because I measured instead of trusting the estimate.

**Correction 2 — a Mac-derived speedup ratio did not transfer.** After optimizing, island was
74% of per-nonce cost on an M-series Mac, so I claimed Jacobian coordinates would give a
further 2.6×. On `zan5` the same probe put island at only 44%, capping that path at ~1.6×. I
withdrew the 2.6× figure rather than carry it forward.

**Correction 3 — memory bandwidth, not cores, is the ceiling.** Scaling 80 → 118 workers moved
per-worker cost from 1.95 s to 2.33 s/nonce: +47% cores bought only ~23% throughput. Each
nonce streams 13.3M ops × 56 B × ~13 batches ≈ 8.9 GB, so 118 workers demand ~450 GB/s. The
real remaining lever is packing the 56-byte `Op` (qubit ids fit u16, bit ids u32, kind u8)
for ~3.5× less traffic — not more cores and not more ECC tuning.

**Correction 4 — a mis-factored frontier.** I initially assumed an intermediate frontier was
`Q=1278`; it was actually `Q=1277` with higher Toffoli. That mattered: it revealed the qubit
axis was not frozen, and that the competing move had been a qubit-for-Toffoli trade at
3,530 Toffoli/qubit against a ~735 break-even.

**Discarded result.** An earlier hunt on the then-current `ce60e68` produced a verified clean
win at 1,204,145,873. Before it could be submitted the frontier moved to `cc82b18`
(−0.296%), superseding it. I dropped it rather than submit a now-worse score, re-based onto
`cc82b18`, and confirmed the ladder step still stacked — the previous rung (MUL 697→696) had
in fact already been absorbed into `cc82b18`.

**Hunt statistics.** 22,300 nonces screened before the hit at 910000024466, against an
expected ~39,800. Waiting is memoryless, so this is an unremarkable draw
(`P(no hit by 22,300) = e^(−0.56) ≈ 57%`).

    score.json  : {"score": 1200544254, "toffoli": 939393, "qubits": 1278}

The source-edit build and the env-var build used during the hunt produce a byte-identical

Delta vs `cc82b18`: **−489,474 (−0.041%)**, entirely on the Toffoli axis
(939,776.350 → 939,392.941); `Q` unchanged at 1278.

## 10. Caveats

- The measured `avg_tof` for a tier depends slightly on which clean nonce is found
  (σ ≈ 28 at 9024 shots), because the nonce reseeds the test island. The tier's *static*
  prediction was 939,388.5; this particular nonce landed at 939,392.9, costing ~4 avg Toffoli
  (~5,100 score) of nonce lottery relative to the tier mean.
- λ per tier rests on 20 draws; the means are indicative, not tight. In particular the
  non-monotonicity between tiers 693 and 692 should be treated as noise until more draws exist.
- pp-hunt is a prefilter and its verdict is not authoritative. Every claim here rests on a
  full `eval_circuit` run, and the tool was gated against `eval_circuit` on four nonces plus
  two independently known-clean baked nonces before use.
- This is a truncation win, so it consumes λ budget: it makes the *next* rung harder, and
  that cost is real and paid by whoever grinds after this.

## 11. Learning

The score has two factors with completely different geometry. `Q` is quantized in ~256-wide
units and perfectly packed (I verified 1278 distinct ids for max id 1277, zero gaps, every
high-index qubit live for 70–91% of the stream), so moving it requires restructuring. The
Toffoli axis, by contrast, is a plateau you descend in fixed ~383-Toffoli half-round steps
whose gain is linear while the clean-nonce cost is exponential (λ slope ≈ +1.7 per full round
here, so ≈ ×2.3 search cost per half-step). Those are not interchangeable directions, and the
right tool differs: the Toffoli ladder is a rejection-sampling problem where throughput is
everything, while the qubit axis needs an actual algorithmic idea.

The corollary that shaped this session: producing better candidates was never the bottleneck —
validation was. A ladder sweep took minutes; the clean nonce took the entire budget.

## 12. Next steps

1. Pack the `Op` struct 56 B → 16 B for ~3.5× less memory traffic; this is the only remaining
   large multiplier on hunt throughput on this host and it makes tier 694 (−0.079%) about a
   1.2-hour job instead of ~4 hours.
2. Then tier 694 is the last economically reachable rung on this host; 693/692 need either the
   packing plus more machines, or a lower-λ circuit.
3. Higher leverage than either: reduce λ itself. The classical failure channel is dominated by
   the convergence tail, so any change that tightens convergence buys ladder depth
   multiplicatively (each −1.0 λ multiplies hunt yield by e).
4. Re-derive whether the qubit axis can go to 1277 *while* holding this depth — the two axes
   were traded against each other twice today by different parties, which suggests the joint
   optimum has not been found.
